what.question: What is Mochi?
what.answer: Mochi is a period tracker app for iPhone with a cute mascot. It predicts your next period, reminds you when to change your pad and rewards daily check-ins with 12 collectible flavors.

free.question: Is Mochi free?
free.answer: Yes. Cycle tracking, predictions, the pad change reminder, moods, streaks and starter flavors are free. Mochi Plus is optional.

private.question: Is my period data private?
private.answer: Yes. Period dates, flow, symptoms and moods stay on your iPhone by default, unless you enable optional backup. They are never sent to analytics, logs or crash reports. Our privacy policy explains how optional backup works.

offline.question: Does Mochi work without an account or internet?
offline.answer: Yes. Every core feature works offline and no account is required. An account is optional if you want backup and sync.

reminder.question: How does the pad change reminder work?
reminder.answer: Choose a day pad, overnight pad or liner and a duration from 2 to 8 hours. Mochi counts down on Home, in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen.

lockScreen.question: Will my Lock Screen show that I'm on my period?
lockScreen.answer: No. The Live Activity uses private, discreet wording and never states that you are on your period.

medical.question: Can I use Mochi as birth control?
medical.answer: No. Mochi's predictions are estimates for period awareness, not contraception, diagnosis or medical advice.

PrivacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
PrivacyPolicy.intro: Your cycle is yours. Here’s exactly what Mochi keeps on your iPhone and what it never shares.
PrivacyPolicy.heroAlt: A happy pink Mochi wrapped in a cozy blanket, hugging a pink iPhone with a heart padlock on its screen
PrivacyPolicy.callout: Period dates, flow, symptoms, moods, sex, tests and pregnancy logs never leave your iPhone unless you turn on backup.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: Mochi collects only what you choose to add: period dates, flow, symptoms, moods, sex, tests and pregnancy logs. Mochi uses them on your iPhone for predictions, reminders, streaks and collectible flavors.
collect.detail: You don’t need an account. If you create one to turn on backup, we keep your email address (with Sign in with Apple, the address Apple shares with us, which can be a private relay address) and, if you sign up with email, a password. We also collect app usage data and, if you subscribe, your purchase history, as described below.

device.title: What stays on your iPhone
device.body: Your cycle data lives in a local database on your iPhone. It’s used only by Mochi to show your cycle, make predictions and keep your streaks and flavors.
device.detail: You stay in control. Your data is not sent to analytics, logs or crash reports. It only leaves your iPhone if you choose to turn on backup, in which case it’s encrypted and linked only to you.

analytics.title: Never in analytics
analytics.body: We use PostHog, on servers in the EU, to understand how Mochi is used: app opens, screen names, onboarding steps and simple counts, such as how many fields a check-in filled. PostHog also receives standard technical details: device model, iOS and app version, and an approximate location derived from your IP address.
analytics.detail: Your period dates, flow, symptoms, moods, sex, tests and pregnancy logs are never included in analytics, logs or crash reports. Usage data is linked to a random app identifier, and to your account ID if you sign in. It is never used for advertising or to track you across other apps and websites. Crash and performance reports from Apple’s MetricKit are aggregated by iOS and stay on your iPhone.

backup.title: Backup and sync
backup.body: Backup is optional. If you turn it on, your account and your backup are stored with Supabase, on servers in the EU (Frankfurt). Your cycle entries are encrypted on your iPhone before they are uploaded, with a key kept in your iCloud Keychain, so the server only stores data it cannot read.
backup.detail: You can use Mochi’s core features offline and without an account. Your cycle data stays on your iPhone unless you choose backup.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.body: Mochi Plus is an optional subscription, and the free core features keep working without it. Apple handles payment: we never see your card details.
subscriptions.detail: We use RevenueCat to check whether your subscription is active. RevenueCat receives your App Store purchase history (products, purchase and renewal dates) linked to an anonymous ID, or to your account ID if you are signed in. It never receives your cycle entries.

providers.title: Who helps us run Mochi
providers.body: We share data only with the services that run Mochi, each limited to what it needs: Supabase (account and encrypted backup, EU), PostHog (usage analytics, EU), RevenueCat (subscription status) and Apple (App Store purchases, Sign in with Apple and iCloud Keychain).
providers.detail: These providers process data on our behalf under their data processing terms. We don’t sell your data or share it with advertisers or data brokers.

waitlist.title: If you join the launch waitlist
waitlist.body: If you leave your email on our website to hear when Mochi reaches the App Store, we store that address, the language of the page and the date you signed up. It's kept with Supabase, on servers in the EU.
waitlist.detail: We use it only to send you one email when Mochi launches, then delete the list. It's never shared, sold or used for advertising. To be removed sooner, email us at the address below.

deletion.title: Delete your account and data
deletion.body: You can delete your account at any time in the app: Settings › Privacy & data › Delete account. This deletes your account and all your backed-up data from our servers straight away, and erases Mochi’s data from your iPhone.
deletion.detail: Not signed in? Settings › Privacy & data › Delete all data erases everything Mochi keeps on your iPhone. Deleting your account doesn’t cancel a subscription: manage that in your Apple ID settings. To also have your usage data and purchase records removed from PostHog and RevenueCat, email us and we’ll do it within 30 days.

rights.title: You stay in control
rights.body: You decide what information to add to Mochi. All core features work without creating an account or enabling backup.
rights.detail: Under the GDPR you can ask to access, correct, export or delete your information, or object to how it’s used. You can export your entries in the app (Settings › Privacy & data › Export my data) and delete them yourself. For anything else, email us. You can also complain to your data protection authority.

children.title: Children’s privacy
children.body: The same privacy approach applies to cycle entries: they stay on the iPhone unless optional backup is enabled.
children.detail: If you are a parent or guardian with a question about privacy, please contact us. Avoid including sensitive health information in your message.

contact.title: Let’s talk about privacy
contact.body: Questions about this policy or how Mochi handles your information? We’re here to help.
contact.detail: Please avoid including period dates, symptoms or other health information in your message.

bestWay.question: What is the best way to track my period?
bestWay.answer: Choose a method you can use consistently: a period app, calendar, or notebook. Record when bleeding starts and ends, its heaviness, and any symptoms you want to follow. Reviewing your entries can help you notice patterns and changes.

meaning.question: What does “tracking period” mean?
meaning.answer: Period tracking means recording your bleeding dates and related symptoms over time. Day 1 is the first day of your period. Cycle length is counted from that day to the day before your next period starts.

noBleeding.question: How do I track my menstrual cycle if I don't bleed?
noBleeding.answer: You can keep a dated symptom and mood diary, but symptoms alone cannot reliably confirm ovulation or your cycle phase. Some hormonal contraception changes bleeding and ovulation. If pregnancy is possible, take a pregnancy test. Seek medical advice if you miss three periods in a row, or sooner if you are concerned.

whenToStart.question: When should you start tracking your period?
whenToStart.answer: You can start recording periods from your first one, or at any later time. Begin with the bleeding dates you know and keep adding entries. If you start midway through a cycle, leave uncertain dates blank instead of guessing.

PeriodCalculator.disclaimer: These dates are estimates and may differ from your actual cycle. Do not use this calculator as a method of contraception or to diagnose a health condition.

how.title: How the calculator works
how.first: Your next period date is calculated by adding your average menstrual cycle length to the first day of your last period. For example, if your last period started on 1 March and your cycle usually lasts 28 days, your next period is estimated to start on 29 March. The calculator repeats this calculation for your upcoming cycles and uses your usual period length to estimate when each period may end.
how.second: Your estimated ovulation date is calculated by counting back 14 days from the predicted start of your next period. According to Cleveland Clinic, the luteal phase, which follows ovulation, lasts about 14 days. Your estimated fertile window includes the five days before this estimated ovulation date and the day itself. Ovulation can happen earlier or later than predicted, so these dates cannot confirm when you are fertile.
how.third: A 28-day cycle is a useful starting point, but your own cycle may be different. The US Office on Women's Health gives a normal adult cycle range of 24 to 38 days, while Cleveland Clinic gives a range of 21 to about 35 days. Using your actual average cycle length makes the calculation more personal. Everything is calculated directly in your browser. Your period dates are never stored or sent to a server.

faq.title: Questions about calculating your next period

next.question: How do I calculate my next period?
next.answer: Add your average cycle length to the first day of your last period to estimate when your next period will start. Your cycle length is the number of days from the first day of one period to the first day of the next.

ovulation.question: How do I calculate my ovulation date and fertile window?
ovulation.answer: Count back about 14 days from your estimated next period date to calculate your likely ovulation date. The estimated fertile window includes the five days before ovulation and the estimated ovulation day itself. These dates cannot confirm ovulation and should not be used as contraception.

accuracy.question: How accurate is a next period calculator?
accuracy.answer: A period calculator provides an estimate based on your usual cycle length, rather than an exact prediction. Estimates may be less reliable during adolescence, after a recent pregnancy, while breastfeeding, when using hormonal contraception or during periods of stress. If your period is late and you could be pregnant, take a pregnancy test and speak to a doctor or nurse.

irregular.question: Can I calculate my next period if I have irregular cycles?
irregular.answer: Yes, you can use your average cycle length to estimate your next period, but the result may be less reliable if your cycles are irregular. Tracking your actual period dates over several months can help you understand your usual pattern. Speak to a doctor or nurse if your cycles are often shorter than 24 days or longer than 38 days.

OvulationCalculator.disclaimer: These dates are estimates based on an average cycle and may differ from when you actually ovulate. Do not use this calculator as contraception. If you're trying to get pregnant and have concerns, talk to a doctor or nurse.

how.title: How the ovulation calculator works
how.first: The calculator first estimates when your next period will start by adding your average cycle length to the first day of your last period. Ovulation usually happens about 14 days before a period starts, because the luteal phase that follows ovulation lasts around 14 days, according to Cleveland Clinic. So in a 28-day cycle, ovulation is estimated around day 14, and in a 32-day cycle, around day 18.
how.second: After ovulation, the egg can be fertilised for about 12 to 24 hours, but sperm can survive in the body for up to five days. That's why the fertile window shown here covers the five days before your estimated ovulation and the ovulation day itself. The two days before ovulation and ovulation day are highlighted as your most fertile days, because that's when the chance of pregnancy is highest.
how.third: Your cycle can change from month to month, so ovulation may happen earlier or later than estimated, especially if your cycles are irregular. Tracking your periods, watching your cervical mucus or using ovulation tests can give you a clearer picture. Everything is calculated in your browser: your dates are never stored or sent to a server.

faq.title: Questions about ovulation and your fertile window

calculate.question: How do I calculate my ovulation date?
calculate.answer: Subtract 14 days from the date you expect your next period to start. For example, if your cycle lasts 30 days and your last period started on 1 March, your next period is due around 31 March, so ovulation is estimated around 17 March. This is an estimate, because the time between ovulation and your period can vary slightly.

fertile.question: How long is the fertile window?
fertile.answer: The fertile window usually lasts about six days: the five days before ovulation and the day of ovulation. Sperm can survive for up to five days, while the egg lives for about 12 to 24 hours after it's released, so sex in the days before ovulation can lead to pregnancy.

signs.question: What are the signs of ovulation?
signs.answer: Common signs include clear, slippery and stretchy cervical mucus (similar to raw egg white), a small rise in basal body temperature after ovulation, mild pain on one side of the lower belly and a higher sex drive. Ovulation tests detect the rise in luteinising hormone (LH) that happens about 24 to 36 hours before ovulation.

irregular.question: Does the ovulation calculator work with irregular cycles?
irregular.answer: It can give a rough estimate, but it's less reliable when your cycle length changes a lot from month to month. Tracking your periods for a few months, watching for signs of ovulation or using ovulation tests can help. Speak to a doctor if your cycles are often shorter than 24 days or longer than 38 days, or if you've been trying to get pregnant for a year (six months if you're 35 or older).

contraception.question: Can I use an ovulation calculator to avoid pregnancy?
contraception.answer: No. A calendar estimate can't tell you exactly when you ovulate, and ovulation can shift from one cycle to the next, so no day can be guaranteed safe. If you want to avoid pregnancy, talk to a doctor, nurse or pharmacist about reliable contraception.
